slices.focus: Tasha discovers community-history documentaries as ideal tired-evening viewing
slices.summary: During a calmer stretch, Tasha attends Imani's library documentary night in Cary and discovers she is especially drawn to intimate community-history films — local stories told through elders on porches and in church basements. She realizes this niche matches her tired-evening needs perfectly: low stimulation, no emotional overload, affordable, and easy to access. The agent helps her plan a short watchlist organized into three categories (tired-evening, weekend-attention, social-watch), a light ritual (tea, phone away, one film), and a body-awareness test (notice if jaw eases, mind stops racing after 20 minutes). Tasha plans to text Imani appreciation and curate her list.
